title: The Golden Lily fire
summary: Punch tells of six or eight years at the Golden Lily until a fire, and the owner buying new instruments.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. I didn't wait for two Sundays ago. See I had a steady job, I worked at Golden Lily, see. We worked there six years, you know. Six, eight years, Golden Lily. And we'd have been there longer, but one Saturday night we all played to two o'clock. And went home and a cab driver come by my house and said, hey Punch, see, you're honing the Golden Lily? I said, yeah, why? Golden Lily on fire. Boy. Rambling around there, trying to get them, we couldn't get them. But the guy was white with a China man, Fugger Nick. Man, he got everybody a brand new instrument. He got a drum, bass and everything.
Well that's what you really call getting fired, huh?
Did you go back there and for the fixer place?

No, he didn't never open up no more. He left. I don't know what come after him, see. He passed out, nobody knew where he died, there's nothing. I guess people say you never know when a Chinaman died, but that's one I didn't know when he died, he just went on off somewhere.
